messages:
mira: Short thread: proposal for progressive decrypt+streaming dequant pipeline for encrypted safetensors. goal: warmup fast without materializing full decrypted checkpoint on disk. looking for tradeoffs.

paul: sounds good. what's the core flow you imagine?

mira: ingest produces encrypted shard objects (AES-GCM per-shard) with KMS-wrapped keys. runtime should be able to request a presigned range + wrapped-key, stream-decrypt chunk-by-chunk into a decrypt buffer, and optionally apply a dequant step on the fly (qint8->fp16) before writing to hotcache. no full-file temp files.

chen: important constraints: HSM/KMS ops are rate-limited. we can't call UnwrapKey per 10MB chunk. unwrap should happen once per shard session and we should derive a streaming key with a local ephemeral key-encrypting-key (EEK).

keymgr-bot: policy note: unwrap quota for project "redwood-ml" is 2500/hour; recommend caching unwrap tokens for up to 1h.

paul: okay so sequence: 1) runtime obtains commit metadata (includes wrapped-shard-key-id + signature), 2) runtime requests UnwrapKey (once) -> gets plaintext key sealed in memory, 3) use that key to perform AES-GCM streaming decryption for ranges, 4) apply dequant on decode path if requested by route.

mira: yes. add protections: ephemeral key held in secure allocator and zeroed after session, restrict lifetime via EEK TTL. also attach a per-session HMAC of ranges accessed so audit can show which parts were read.

chen: audit HMAC is nice, but computing HMAC per-range means extra CPU. maybe compute a single session HMAC that accumulates range digests: session_hmac = HMAC(session_key, concat(range_sha256s)). cheap since range_sha256s computed as part of streaming integrity.

paul: streaming integrity: AES-GCM already provides per-chunk integrity. but we want to verify decrypted bytes align with tensor boundaries. idea: ingest writes per-tensor canonical checksums in index; runtime can compare running digest per tensor while streaming.

mira: yes, reuse the tensor-index sidecar. ingress must include encryption_meta per-shard: {wrapped_key_id, iv_prefix, chunk_size, tensors:[{name, offset, length, sha256}]}. runtime maps range reads to tensors and validates.

chen: dequant tradeoffs: doing dequant on-the-fly halves storage I/O (store q8), but CPU overhead during warmup increases. we should be able to pick per-route policies: cold-start-aggressive (dequant at ingest -> store fp16 derived artifact), lazy-route (dequant on-the-fly only for pinned layers).

mira: agreed. metadata should carry 'dequant_capabilities': ["runtime-dequant","derived-fp16"], and a cost_estimate: {dequant_ms_per_mb, io_mb_saved}. scheduler can pick based on SLO.

sre: operational concerns: streaming decrypt + dequant will increase CPU and memory. we need metrics: decrypt_cpu_ms, dequant_cpu_ms, peak_alloc_bytes, unwrap_kms_calls. plus alarms if decrypt latency spikes.

paul: encryption edgecases: what about partial-range requests where GCM tag covers whole ciphertext? For AES-GCM you need the tag per message; prefer per-chunk GCM tags so each chunk is independently verifiable. ingest must write chunk-level tags.

mira: yes we standardize on chunked AES-GCM with fixed chunk_size (e.g., 8MB) and tag appended to chunk. chunk offsets in index are chunk-aligned or index maps tensors to chunk ranges. runtime reads chunk(s) and decrypts independently.

chen: padding & alignment: when decrypting a chunk that contains many small tensors, we still compute per-tensor digest as bytes stream crosses tensor boundaries. keep an internal buffer to assemble partial tensors before digesting.

paul: fallback: if runtime can't do dequant on-the-fly (CPU starved), it should request a derived_fp16 artifact from catalog. catalog can lazily derive fp16 by spawning a derivation job that does decrypt->dequant->upload. runtime can wait or fall back to an older checkpoint.

mira: derivation job must have same signing + KMS policy so derived artifacts are tracked back to canonical checkpoint id. and derived artifacts have their own signature referencing parent checkpoint.

keymgr-bot: note: KMS policy for derivation jobs requires that wrapped_key_id be accessible by job-service-role. ensure least-privilege roles.

paul: another security note: streaming exposes ranges via presigned URLs; include short TTL and require session HMAC in range request headers to tie caller to unwrap session. reject range requests without valid session HMAC.

chen: perf optimization: memory mapping decrypted pages into a reuse buffer that can be shared across concurrent requests for same shard session. need reference-counted secure buffers. zero-on-free. watch GC.

sre: engineering ops: we'll need a stress test rig that simulates thousands of concurrent warmups with decrypt+dequant pipeline to measure CPU per-request and KMS unwrap saturation. add a canary for key unwrap rate.

mira: okay next steps: 1) draft ingest extension to include encryption_meta + per-chunk tags + per-tensor checksums, 2) runtime prototype that unwraps once, streams-decrypt chunks, validates tensor checksums, and optionally dequants on the fly, 3) derive-job definition for creating fp16 artifacts, 4) SLO policy to pick runtime vs derive path.

paul: I'll prototype unwrap caching + session HMAC.

chen: I'll take dequant microbenchmark and memory-secure-buffer lib.

sre: I'll draft stress test and KMS quota monitoring.

mira: sweet. please note migration: mark legacy encrypted shards without chunk-tags as "non-streamable" and force full decrypt -> materialize path for them until re-ingested. will add that to RFC. thanks all.
